q: Customers log in to the portal but cannot see their own cases. How do you troubleshoot it?
alt: Portal users see an empty case list, what would you check?
Customer community user can't see cases on their account
My cases page shows nothing for external users
customers cannot view their cases in community
a: I check access layer by layer while logged in as that user. First, object and field access: does the external profile or permission set have Read on Case and the fields shown? Second, record access: for Customer Community users there are no roles, so a sharing set must include their profile and map Case to the user's account or contact, for example User Contact.Account equals Case Account. Third, the data itself: do the cases actually have the AccountId or ContactId filled in? Cases created by an integration often miss the contact. Fourth, the page: is the list view filter "My cases" when the cases are owned by agents? For example, at an appliance company, the sharing set mapped on Contact but cases came in from Email-to-Case without a matched contact, so the fix was in the data, not the setup.

q: When you click Enable Customer User on a contact, you get an error that the portal account owner must have a role. What do you do?
alt: Error portal account owner must have a role, how to fix?
Cannot create partner user because account owner has no role
Why does enabling a community user fail?
portal account owner role error
a: This error means the account's owner has no role in the role hierarchy, and Salesforce needs one to place the external user's portal role under that owner. The fix is to give the account owner a role, or change the account owner to an internal user who has one. For example, if accounts were loaded by an integration user without a role, every new dealer account fails this way, so I either assign that integration user a role or, better, reassign those accounts to the real channel managers who do have roles. I also keep an eye on ownership skew: I do not put thousands of portal accounts under one owner, because that slows down sharing recalculation. The rule mainly matters for role-based licenses like Partner Community and Customer Community Plus.

Fix by assigning a role or changing the owner

q: A customer user must see all the records of other users in the same account, not just their own. How do you set this up?
alt: Customer community user needs to see colleagues' cases
How do users from the same company see each other's records in the portal?
Share records across users of the same account in Experience Cloud
see records of others in same account
a: The answer depends on the license. For Customer Community users, who have no roles, I use a sharing set that maps the user's Contact.Account to the record's Account field. Then every user on that account sees every record linked to the account, no matter who created it. If only some users, like a company admin, should see everything while others see only their own, I either use Customer Community Plus with roles, where the Manager or Executive role sees the User role's records, or super user access for that person. For example, at an office-supplies company, the buying team at one client needs to see all orders for their company: a sharing set on the custom Order object with Account mapped to the user's account solves it, with Read Only or Read/Write access as needed.

q: In a partner portal, the partner's sales manager should see all deals of their company, but each sales rep only their own. How do you design this?
alt: Partner manager needs to see team opportunities
How do partner roles work for executives and reps?
Different visibility inside one partner account
partner role hierarchy setup
a: I use partner roles. When a partner account is enabled, Salesforce creates up to three roles under the account owner, typically Executive, Manager and User, and I choose how many in the Digital Experiences settings. I give the reps the User role and the sales manager the Manager role, with the external OWD on Opportunity set to Private. Because roles roll up, the manager automatically sees opportunities owned by the reps below, and reps see only their own and what is shared with them. q: A guest user creates a record through a public form and then needs to update it in the next step. How do you handle this in Apex safely?
alt: Guest user needs to update a record they just created

Multi-step guest form update record Apex

a: Guests cannot edit records, and once the record is saved it belongs to the default owner, so the guest cannot even read it. The update has to run in system mode, which means a without sharing class, and that is risky, so I keep it as small as possible. My controller stays with sharing, and only one private inner class runs without sharing for the single update. I never trust an Id sent from the browser alone: I return a random token when the record is created, store it on the record, and require that token plus the Id for the update, only within a short time window. For example, on a home-insurance quote form, step one creates the lead and step two adds the property details, so the update method only touches those few fields.

q: Leads from the website must go to the right partner by region, and if a partner does not act within two days the lead should go to another partner. How would you design it?

a: I would split it into routing, acceptance and escalation. For routing, a record-triggered flow or lead assignment rules check the region and assign the lead to that region's partner queue, where partner users are members. Partners see the lead in a lead list or the lead inbox on Partner Central and accept it, which makes them the owner. For escalation, a scheduled path on the flow runs two days after assignment: if the lead is still owned by the queue, or its status has not moved, the flow reassigns it to a backup partner queue and notifies the channel manager. For example, a security-camera maker routes a Texas lead to the Southwest partners' queue; nobody accepts in 48 hours, so it moves to the next partner automatically. I report on accept time per partner to keep it fair.

q: Two partners register the same deal for the same end customer. How would you handle channel conflict?

a: I catch it at submission and decide it in an approval. When a partner registers a deal, the registration flow checks for an open registration with the same end-customer company and similar product, using matching rules on a normalized company name or website. If a match exists, the new registration is flagged and routed to the channel manager instead of being auto-approved. The first-come rule is the usual default, but the channel manager can consider who has the relationship. Approved registrations get an expiry date, so a partner cannot hold a deal forever without progress. For example, two IT resellers both submit "Acme Hospital, 200 laptops": the second one is flagged, the manager sees both side by side, approves the first, and the second partner gets a rejection with the reason. Partners never see each other's registrations.

a: I check the usual causes in order. First, the right bundle type: enhanced LWR sites use DigitalExperienceBundle, while Aura and older LWR sites use ExperienceBundle, and for Aura sites the ExperienceBundle Metadata API setting must be on in both orgs. A common trap is creating the site manually in the target org first: a new LWR site there will be enhanced, so deploying a non-enhanced site on top of it fails on the type mismatch. Second, dependencies: Network and CustomSite must be in the package, plus navigation menus, audiences, Apex, LWCs and profiles. Third, missing content: CMS items and some settings like members or email templates may need manual steps. For example, a team created an empty "Partners" site in production "to save time", and the deploy failed; renaming that site and freeing its URL let the real deploy create it correctly.

q: The security team asks you to audit a public Experience Cloud site before go-live. What do you check?

a: I check what an anonymous person could reach, then what a logged-in user could reach. For guests: the guest profile should have only Read and Create on needed objects, minimal fields, API access off, and no extra Apex class or Visualforce access. I run the Guest User Sharing Rule Access Report and review every guest sharing rule. Then I check trusted sites, clickjack protection, and that "Let guest users see other members" is off unless needed. For logged-in users, I test as a real external user from two different accounts to confirm one cannot see the other's data. Finally I run Health Check and fix findings before launch.

a: Every external user needs a contact on an account, so with individuals I have two choices. Person accounts are the cleanest: each customer is one account-contact record, and they can be enabled as Customer Community users directly. q: A company has two brands with different customers. Would you build one Experience Cloud site or two?

When do you create separate communities?

a: I decide based on how different the users, branding and access are. If both brands share the same users, processes and mostly the same pages, one site with audiences and branding sets is easier to maintain. If they have different customers, different domains, different login pages and legal terms, two sites are cleaner, and they can still share LWCs, Apex and CMS content through channels. Sharing is org-wide, so two sites do not separate data by themselves; I still need sharing sets or rules that keep each brand's customers to their own records. For example, a kitchenware group with a premium brand and a budget brand would build two sites on their own domains with separate login pages, reuse the same case LWC, and share CMS articles where they overlap. q: Walk me through the patient journey in Health Cloud from start to finish.

The referral comes in as a Clinical Service Request, or she starts as a lead from a web form and gets converted. She becomes a person account, with her medical record number stored on the Identifier object, and we record her consent. Then we link her household and caregiver and set up her care team. The care manager runs an assessment, and the answers suggest problems and goals for a care plan built from a template. Appointments are booked through Intelligent Appointment Management. Her conditions, labs and medications flow in from the EHR into the FHIR-aligned clinical data model, usually through MuleSoft. The team monitors her on the timeline and through care gaps. a: The PGI library is the reusable catalog of Problems, Goals and Interventions that care plan templates are built from. Say a clinic manages heart failure patients. ProblemGoalDefinition links problems to goals, since one goal can serve many problems. A CarePlanTemplate then arranges these into a structure. When a care manager creates a plan for a real patient, the definitions turn into records on that patient: problems become HealthCondition records and goals become GoalAssignment records. The plan is saved as a CarePlan record, goals become GoalAssignment records, and interventions from action plan templates become tasks for the team. Over the next weeks the team completes tasks, records outcomes and updates goal progress, while CRM Analytics dashboards show plan status and overdue tasks. How does Health Cloud find missing preventive care?
What is a CareGap record?
care gap closure process
a: A care gap is a recommended service a patient should have had but hasn't, like a diabetic patient with no eye exam in the last year. In Health Cloud the rule is defined as a ClinicalMeasure with its criteria. A care manager clicks New Care Gap on the care gap FlexCard, which runs an OmniScript that evaluates the measure against the patient's data, and if the measure isn't met, a CareGap record is created. Gaps can also be imported from a quality or analytics system, or entered manually. From the gap, the care manager can create a care plan or arrange the missing service. Once the eye exam happens and the data comes in, re-evaluating the measure closes the gap. Payers care a lot about this because closed gaps drive quality scores, so I'd also report on open gaps by provider or program.

q: What is the difference between a ClinicalEncounter and an appointment in Health Cloud?
alt: Encounter vs appointment in Health Cloud, when is each used?
Is a visit stored as ClinicalEncounter or ServiceAppointment?
How do you model visits and hospital stays in Health Cloud?
clinical encounter versus service appointment
a: A ClinicalEncounter is the clinical record of a visit or stay that happened or is happening, while an appointment is the scheduling record for a planned time slot. Say a patient books a cardiology visit for Tuesday at 10. That booking is a ServiceAppointment when scheduling runs on Salesforce Scheduler or Field Service, or a slot in the EHR's schedule. On Tuesday the EHR records the actual visit, and it comes into Health Cloud as a ClinicalEncounter with a status like In Progress or Finished, start and end dates, the facility, and related diagnosis and provider records. Encounters also cover hospital stays, with an admission source and a discharge disposition. So I use appointments for access, booking and no-show reporting, and encounters for clinical history and follow-up logic like 'discharged yesterday'.

q: What are CodeSet and CodeSetBundle in Health Cloud, and why are they needed?
alt: How are medical codes like ICD-10 or SNOMED stored in Health Cloud?
Why does HealthCondition point to a CodeSetBundle?
Explain code sets in the clinical data model.
code set bundle health cloud
a: CodeSet stores a single code from a coding system, and CodeSetBundle groups equivalent codes from different systems, so one clinical concept is referenced once. Say a patient has type 2 diabetes. The EHR might send an ICD-10 code, while the problem list uses SNOMED. Each code is a CodeSet record, and a CodeSetBundle groups them as the same concept. Clinical records point to the bundle; for example HealthCondition.ConditionCodeId is a required lookup to CodeSetBundle, and MedicationStatement can point to CodeSetBundle through MedicationCodeId, or to a Medication record instead. The benefit is that queries and reports work on one concept regardless of which coding system the source used. The gotcha on projects is load order: code sets must be loaded before the clinical data, or inserts fail because the code lookup is required.

q: What do you consider before using Shield Platform Encryption on patient data?
alt: Should we encrypt all PHI fields in Health Cloud?
Deterministic vs probabilistic encryption for patient data.
What breaks when you turn on Platform Encryption?
shield encryption health cloud trade offs
a: Shield Platform Encryption protects PHI at rest, but every encrypted field has a cost, so I encrypt deliberately rather than everything. Say a clinic wants to encrypt date of birth, a national ID number and clinical notes. With probabilistic encryption you can't filter or sort on the field in SOQL, list views or reports, which breaks things like finding a patient by date of birth. Deterministic encryption allows exact-match filtering, so I use it for fields people search on. Encryption also limits some formulas, report features and matching rules, so I retest automation and integrations after enabling it. I check which standard Health Cloud fields support encryption and plan key management, like tenant secret rotation and Bring Your Own Key if required. And encryption isn't access control: a user with read access still sees the decrypted value, so sharing and field-level security still matter.

q: What is the difference between field history tracking, Field Audit Trail and Event Monitoring for patient data?

a: They answer different audit questions. Field history tracking records who changed a field and when, for a limited number of fields and a limited time. Field Audit Trail, part of Shield, extends change history to more fields and keeps it for years, which suits medical record retention rules. Event Monitoring records activity, like who viewed a record, ran or exported a report, called the API, or logged in. Say a patient complains that her allergy list was changed and that someone looked at her chart without reason. The allergy change shows in field history or Field Audit Trail; the chart view shows in Event Monitoring, for example in LightningUriEvent records. So for a HIPAA access audit, history tracking alone isn't enough, because reading a record isn't a change.

q: Write a scheduled Apex job that creates follow-up tasks for patients discharged yesterday.
alt: How do you query discharged encounters and create tasks in Apex?
Automate post-discharge follow-up calls with Apex.
Schedulable class on ClinicalEncounter example.
discharge follow up task apex
a: I find encounters that finished yesterday and create one follow-up task per patient for the patient's owner, usually the care coordinator. Say a hospital wants a call within 48 hours of every discharge. A scheduled job runs each morning, queries ClinicalEncounter for status Finished and an EndDate of yesterday, and inserts tasks due tomorrow. Before inserting, it checks for an open follow-up task so a rerun doesn't create duplicates. In a real build I'd also exclude dispositions like transfer to hospice using DischargeDispositionId, switch to Batch Apex if volumes are large, and if the EHR sends discharges in near real time, a record-triggered flow on the encounter is simpler than a nightly job.
points: ClinicalEncounter: Status Finished + EndDate = YESTERDAY
One task per patient, owned by the patient owner

q: A clinic wants nurses to see only their own patients. How would you set it up?
alt: Nurses should not see patients assigned to other nurses. What do you do?
How do you restrict patient visibility to the assigned nurse?
Each nurse has a panel of patients and should only see those. How?
nurse sees only own patients health cloud
a: I'd make patient records private and then open access only to the assigned nurse. Say a clinic has twelve nurses, each with a panel of patients. Step one, set the Account org-wide default to Private; person accounts already require Contact to be controlled by parent, so the contact side follows. Step two, define what 'own patient' means: the nurse owns the patient record, or there's an assigned nurse field or a care team membership. If the nurse is the owner, Private is enough. If not, automation shares the record with the nurse when she's assigned and removes it when she isn't. Step three, clinical records with a master-detail to the patient follow automatically, but any object with its own sharing needs the same treatment. Step four, make sure nurse permission sets don't have View All, and test by logging in as two different nurses.

q: A hospital sends referrals that must automatically create the patient and start a care plan. How would you design it?
alt: Referral from a hospital must create a patient and a care plan. Walk me through it.
How would you automate referral intake to care plan in Health Cloud?
Inbound referral should create the patient if new and kick off care management. Design it.
referral to patient and care plan automation
a: I'd break it into intake, patient matching, acceptance, then the care plan. Say a hospital refers a heart failure patient to a cardiology practice. First, intake: if the referral arrives over FHIR or HL7, MuleSoft maps it to a ClinicalServiceRequest; if it comes by fax, Intelligent Document Automation extracts it from a Received Document. Second, matching: search the Identifier for the MRN, then name plus date of birth; if there's no match, create a person account, and if the match is weak, send it to a review queue rather than guess. Third, an intake coordinator accepts the referral using the IsAccepted field on the Clinical Service Request. Fourth, a flow assigns a care manager and creates a task, and the care manager uses New Care Plan with the heart failure template. I keep that last step human because the plan needs clinical judgement, while everything before it is automated.
points: Intake: FHIR/HL7 via MuleSoft or fax via Intelligent Document Automation
Match on Identifier (MRN), then demographics; weak matches to review
Accept referral (IsAccepted on ClinicalServiceRequest)
Assign care manager; care plan from template

q: You need to sync allergies from the EHR into Health Cloud. How would you do it?
alt: How would you bring allergy data from Epic into Salesforce?
Design an integration for AllergyIntolerance from the EHR.
The nurses want EHR allergies visible in the patient 360. Steps?
sync allergies ehr fhir health cloud
a: I'd sync them one way, with the EHR as the source of truth, into the standard AllergyIntolerance object. Say a clinic uses Epic and nurses want allergies in the patient 360. Step one, pull the FHIR AllergyIntolerance resource through MuleSoft, for example MuleSoft Direct for Health Cloud or the healthcare accelerator templates. Step two, map the fields: patient to PatientId by finding the account through its Identifier, code to the CodeSetBundle lookup, clinical status to Status, verification status to VerificationStatus, plus severity and category. Step three, use SourceSystemIdentifier as the matching key so repeated messages update the same record instead of duplicating it. Step four, when the EHR marks an allergy entered in error, update the status rather than delete, so the history is clear. Finally, make the object read-only for clinicians in Salesforce, log failures, and alert someone when patient matching fails.

q: Security wants an alert or a block when someone exports a large patient report or mass-extracts patient data. What would you do?
alt: How do you stop users from exporting patient data in bulk?
Use Transaction Security to protect PHI, how?
Compliance wants real-time alerts on data exfiltration in Health Cloud.
transaction security policy report export
a: I'd use Shield Event Monitoring with Transaction Security policies, which act on events in real time. Say a billing user tries to export a report with thousands of patient rows. Step one, turn on the relevant real-time events, mainly ReportEvent, ListViewEvent and ApiEvent. Step two, create a Transaction Security policy on ReportEvent with a condition on the number of rows and the objects the report touches, then pick the action: block it, require multi-factor authentication, or notify the security team. Step three, a similar policy on API events catches mass extraction through tools or integrations. The gotcha: page views in LightningUriEvent can't drive Transaction Security, so for 'someone opened a VIP chart' I query or stream those events and alert separately. I'd tune thresholds with the privacy officer and test in a sandbox, because a policy that's too strict blocks real work.
points: Transaction Security policies on ReportEvent, ListViewEvent, ApiEvent
Actions: block, MFA, notify
LightningUriEvent cannot drive policies: query or stream it
Tune thresholds with compliance, test first

q: Design a prior authorization approval flow where simple requests are auto-approved, nurses review the rest, and only physicians can deny.
alt: Prior authorization approval flow in Health Cloud, how would you build it?
How do you route prior auth requests to nurse and physician reviewers?
Auto-approve some authorization requests and escalate others. Design it.
utilization management review tiers
a: I'd build a tiered review on the Care Request, with the rules kept outside code so the clinical team can change them. Say a provider requests an MRI for a member. Step one, the request lands as a Care Request with Care Request Items for the services and Care Diagnosis records, plus a case for SLA tracking. Step two, check eligibility against the member plan and coverage benefits; if the member isn't covered, route it to a specific queue. Step three, auto-approval rules, for example a decision table on service code, diagnosis and place of service; if every item matches, approve and notify the provider. Step four, everything else goes through Omni-Channel to a nurse reviewer queue, tracked on Care Request Reviewer records. Nurses can approve, but a likely denial escalates to a physician reviewer, because adverse decisions usually need one. Milestones warn before turnaround deadlines, and every decision is logged for appeals.
points: Care Request + Care Request Items + Care Diagnosis + case for SLA
Eligibility from member plan and coverage benefits
Auto-approve via configurable rules (e.g. decision table)

q: Front desk staff should see patient demographics and appointments but not diagnoses or medications. How would you do it?
alt: Hide clinical data from non-clinical users in Health Cloud.
Receptionists must not see diagnoses. What do you configure?
How do you separate clinical and non-clinical access to a patient record?
front desk no access to clinical data
a: I'd control it with object and field permissions, not just page layouts. Say the front desk at a clinic checks people in and books visits. Their permission set gives access to the patient account fields they need, like name, address, phone and insurance, plus appointments, but no object access to clinical objects like HealthCondition, MedicationStatement, AllergyIntolerance and CareObservation. Sensitive fields on the account itself, like a behavioral health flag, get field-level security hidden for them. Then the patient page uses component visibility or Dynamic Forms so they don't see empty clinical sections. Hiding a component alone isn't security, because data can still show in reports, search or list views if permissions allow it. I test by logging in as a front desk user and trying to run a report on conditions to confirm nothing comes back.

Field-level security on sensitive account fields

Test reports, search and list views as the user

q: Duplicate patients keep getting created from the EHR feed and the portal. How would you fix and prevent it?
alt: How do you handle duplicate patient records in Health Cloud?
Patient matching keeps failing and creating duplicates. What would you do?
Two records for the same patient, one from EHR and one from portal. Fix it.
duplicate person accounts health cloud
a: I'd fix the matching logic first, then clean up what's already there. Say a patient registers on the portal as Bob Smith and the EHR later sends Robert Smith with an MRN, and now there are two records. Prevention: the EHR integration matches on the Identifier holding the MRN and its issuing facility before anything else, and clinical records match on SourceSystemIdentifier. Portal registration looks for an existing person account by date of birth plus name or email and links to it instead of creating a new one. Duplicate and matching rules on person accounts catch manual entry. If the organization has an enterprise master patient index, that should be the single source of patient identity. Cleanup: run a duplicate report and merge person accounts after a clinical check, since merging moves related records to the surviving account. Then watch a weekly duplicate report so it doesn't creep back.
points: Match on Identifier (MRN + issuing authority) first
Portal registration links to existing patients
Duplicate and matching rules for manual entry
EMPI as identity source if available
Merge carefully, monitor weekly

q: A hospital wants a follow-up call within 48 hours after every discharge. How would you set it up?
alt: Discharge follow-up: how do you make sure every patient gets a call?
Automate post-discharge outreach in Health Cloud.
What happens in Health Cloud when a patient is discharged?
transition of care follow up call
a: I'd trigger a follow-up task from the encounter that marks the discharge. Say a patient goes home after pneumonia on Monday. The EHR sends the discharge, and the ClinicalEncounter in Health Cloud updates to Finished with an end date and a discharge disposition. A record-triggered flow on ClinicalEncounter fires when the status changes to Finished, checks the disposition to skip cases like death or transfer to another hospital, and creates a task for the patient's care coordinator due within two days. If the task is still open after a day, an escalation alerts the team lead. The call itself can follow a short OmniScript covering medications, symptoms and whether a follow-up visit is booked. Finally, a report shows the percentage of discharges called within 48 hours, which is what the hospital will measure.

q: Patients send blood pressure readings from home devices. The care coordinator must be alerted when a reading is too high. How would you build it?
alt: Remote patient monitoring alerts in Health Cloud, how?
Alert the care team when a vital sign is out of range.
How do you handle device readings and thresholds in Health Cloud?
rpm blood pressure alert care observation
a: I'd store readings as CareObservation records and alert only on out-of-range values, without flooding the coordinator. Say a hypertension program has hundreds of patients each sending two readings a day. Step one, the device platform sends data through an integration; for large volumes I might keep raw readings in Data 360 and bring only abnormal or summary readings into core Health Cloud. Step two, thresholds: a program default, plus a patient-specific target from the care plan goal. Step three, evaluate asynchronously, in the integration layer or an async path of a record-triggered flow, so loading isn't slowed down. Step four, for a high reading, create one task or custom notification for the coordinator, but only if there's no open alert for that patient already. Step five, show the trend on the timeline or a FlexCard chart so the coordinator sees context, not one number.

Evaluate asynchronously

q: A health plan wants to find diabetic members who missed their annual eye exam and get them scheduled. How would you do it?
alt: How would you run a care gap closure campaign in Health Cloud?
Find members missing preventive screenings and reach out.
Payer wants to close quality gaps for diabetic members. Steps?
care gap outreach payer diabetes
a: That's a care gap use case. Say a payer has thousands of members with diabetes. Step one, define a ClinicalMeasure: members with an active diabetes condition and no eye exam in the last twelve months. Step three, outreach: a list view or segment of members with open gaps feeds calls, texts, or an agent that offers in-network eye doctors and open slots. q: A patient withdraws consent to share her data with a program partner. What happens in Health Cloud?
alt: How do you handle consent revocation in Health Cloud?
Patient revokes consent. What must change in the system?
How do you enforce a withdrawn consent across integrations?
consent withdrawal health cloud
a: I treat withdrawal as a recorded event plus enforced behavior, not just a checkbox. Say a patient in a remote monitoring program tells the nurse she no longer wants her data shared with the partner analytics company. Step one, record it: update her Authorization Form Consent for that form, or add a new consent record showing the withdrawal and date, so the history stays intact. Step two, enforce it: integrations and Data 360 activations that send data for that Data Use Purpose check consent status before sending, and stop. Step three, program status: end the enrollment if the program depends on that consent. How do you let a family member see a patient record on Experience Cloud?
Daughter needs to manage her mother's appointments online. Design it.
proxy access caregiver portal health cloud
a: I'd model the daughter as her own person account, link her as caregiver, get the mother's authorization, and then grant access explicitly. On the portal I show only patient-friendly fields.

home health visits field service health cloud

Set up a diabetes care plan template with goals and tasks.
care plan template setup

q: An older Health Cloud org uses the managed-package EHR objects. The client wants to move to the clinical data model. How would you plan it?
alt: Migrate from HealthCloudGA EHR objects to standard clinical objects, how?
How do you move legacy Health Cloud clinical data to the FHIR-aligned model?
Plan a data model migration in Health Cloud.
ehr objects to clinical data model migration
a: I'd run it as a data migration with a parallel period, not a big-bang switch. Say a clinic has years of conditions and medications in the older EHR custom objects from the package. Step one, inventory: which objects and fields are used, and which flows, Apex, reports, timeline settings and integrations touch them. Step four, rebuild pages, Enhanced Timeline definitions, reports and sharing. Step five, run both in parallel, reconcile counts per patient, then retire the old objects. Clinician sign-off on sample patients is my go-live gate.

q: A clinic wants an Agentforce agent on its patient portal that can reschedule appointments. How would you design it safely?
alt: Design an AI agent for patient scheduling in Health Cloud.
How do you build an Agentforce agent that handles PHI safely?
Patients should reschedule through a chatbot. What guardrails do you add?
agentforce patient portal appointment agent
a: I'd keep the agent narrow, grounded and verified. Say patients ask 'Can I move my Thursday appointment?' late at night. q: Developers need realistic test data, but a full sandbox would copy real patient data. What would you do?
alt: How do you handle PHI in sandboxes?
Sandbox refresh for a Health Cloud org with patient data, what precautions?
How do you give developers test data without exposing PHI?
data masking sandbox health cloud
a: Real PHI shouldn't sit in sandboxes where developers and vendors work, so I'd mask it or use synthetic data. Say a health system refreshes a full sandbox for user testing. q: A portal patient reports she can see another patient's appointment. What do you do?
alt: A patient sees someone else's data on the Experience Cloud site. How do you respond?
Data leak on the patient portal, how would you troubleshoot it?
What usually causes portal users to see other users' records?
patient portal privacy breach troubleshooting
a: I treat it as a possible privacy breach first and a bug second. Say a patient emails the clinic a screenshot of someone else's upcoming visit. Step one, contain: involve the privacy officer, and if the cause isn't obvious, disable the affected component or page right away. Step two, find the cause, usually one of a few: a sharing set mapping the wrong field, like a household account instead of the patient's own account; external org-wide defaults set to Public Read; a guest user with record access; or Apex behind an LWC running without sharing or without user mode. Step three, fix it and test with two test patient users side by side. Step four, use Event Monitoring data to see who viewed what during the exposure window, because compliance needs that to decide whether breach notification is required. Step five, add a regression test so it can't come back.
points: Contain first, involve privacy officer

q: What is Salesforce CPQ and what is its current status?

Is CPQ end of life or end of sale?
what is sales force c p q and is it still supported
What replaced Salesforce CPQ?
a: Salesforce CPQ stands for Configure, Price, Quote. It started as the Steelbrick product, and it's a managed package with the SBQQ namespace. Say a rep at a packaging manufacturer is working an opportunity for custom printed boxes. In CPQ they pick a bundle, configure the options, the pricing and discounts get applied, and they generate the quote document straight from the opportunity. On status, the key point is that CPQ is end of sale, not end of life. New customers can't buy it, but existing customers keep support, can renew and add users, and still get critical fixes. They just won't get major new features. The strategic successor is Revenue Cloud Advanced, part of Salesforce Revenue Cloud. It's also been branded Agentforce Revenue Management, and it started out as Revenue Lifecycle Management. So I'd say CPQ skills are still very relevant because so many orgs run it, but new implementations are increasingly going to Revenue Cloud Advanced.
points: Managed package, namespace SBQQ (from the Steelbrick acquisition)
End of sale, not end of life: existing customers stay supported
Maintenance mode: no major new feature development

q: What is a product bundle in Salesforce CPQ, and what are features and options?
alt: Explain bundles, features and options in CPQ
How do you set up a bundle product in CPQ?
what is product feature versus product option in cpq
How is a CPQ bundle structured?
a: A bundle is a parent product that groups other products so the rep configures them together. Say we sell a 'Retail Packaging Service' bundle. The parent product has its Configuration Type set to Required or Allowed, and that's what makes the configurator open. Inside it, Product Features are the categories, like Box Type, Printing and Kitting. A feature controls the layout and the minimum and maximum number of options the rep can pick, so I might say pick exactly one box type. Product Options are the links from the bundle to the actual child products, like a 'Two-colour print' product. Each option holds settings such as default quantity, whether it's selected by default, whether it's required, or whether it's bundled at zero price. The way I remember it: bundle product on top, features grouping the options, and options pointing at the real products.
points: Bundle = parent product with Configuration Type Required or Allowed
Feature = grouping/category with min and max option counts
Option = junction from bundle to a child product with quantity and selection settings

q: On a CPQ product option, what is the difference between Selected, Required and Bundled, and what does Option Type do?
alt: Required vs Selected vs Bundled checkbox on product option
What do Component, Accessory and Related Product option types mean?
how do you make an option mandatory in a cpq bundle
Why does a bundled option show zero price?
a: Selected means the option is ticked by default but the rep can remove it. Required means it's selected and can't be removed, so that's how you make an option mandatory. Bundled means it's included in the parent's price, so the line shows a zero price and the quantity is normally locked. Option Type is about quantity. With Component, the option quantity is multiplied by the bundle quantity. With Accessory and Related Product, the quantity stays independent of the parent. For example, say a packaging bundle includes one pallet wrap per unit as a Component. If the rep quotes two bundles, they get two pallet wraps automatically. But if artwork setup is an Accessory with quantity one, it stays at one whether they quote two bundles or ten. Getting these settings right up front saves you a lot of product rules later.
points: Selected = default on, removable
Required = always on, cannot be removed
Bundled = price included in parent, shows as zero
Component quantity multiplies with bundle quantity; Accessory does not

q: What are option constraints in CPQ and when would you use them instead of product rules?
alt: Explain dependent and exclusive option constraints
How do you stop two options being selected together in a bundle?
option constraint vs product rule cpq
What is an exclusive constraint in Salesforce CPQ?
a: Option constraints are the simple, no-rule way to control which options can be picked together inside one bundle. You create an Option Constraint record that links a constrained option to a constraining option, and you pick a type. Dependent means the constrained option can only be selected after the constraining option is selected. Exclusive means the two can't be selected together. Take a packaging bundle. Foil stamping might be dependent on premium printing, so the rep can't pick foil until premium print is chosen. Single-wall box and double-wall box would be exclusive, because you'd only ever pick one. The catch is that constraints only work inside the same bundle configuration. If I need logic across bundles, conditions on quote-level values, or products added automatically, I move to product rules.
points: Dependent: option B requires option A
Exclusive: options A and B cannot be selected together
Only within the same bundle; use product rules for anything wider

q: What are the types of product rules in Salesforce CPQ?
alt: Explain validation, alert, selection and filter product rules
What product rule types are there in CPQ?
difference between validation rule and alert rule in cpq
What is a selection rule in CPQ?
a: There are four product rule types. Validation rules block the user with an error until the configuration or quote is fixed. Alert rules show a warning but let them carry on. Selection rules automatically add, remove, show, hide, enable or disable options or products. Filter rules dynamically filter the product list used in option search. In a packaging setup I'd use them like this: a validation rule that stops a pallet shipping bundle being saved without at least one wrapping option, an alert that warns the rep about a rush lead time, a selection rule that auto-adds corner protectors, and a filter rule that only shows lids that fit the chosen box size. Each rule also has a scope, Product for the configurator or Quote for the line editor, an evaluation event like Load, Edit, Save or Always, error conditions that decide when it fires, and actions where needed.
points: Validation = hard stop; Alert = warning only
Selection = add/remove/show/hide/enable/disable
Filter = dynamic product search filter
Scope: Product (configurator) or Quote; events: Load, Edit, Save, Always

q: What is the difference between a product rule and a price rule in CPQ?
alt: Product rule vs price rule
When do you use a price rule instead of a product rule?
price rules versus product rules in salesforce cpq
Which CPQ rule changes the price and which controls configuration?
a: Product rules control what's selected or allowed, and price rules control the numbers. A product rule validates, alerts, auto-selects or filters products and options, so it's about the configuration being correct. A price rule changes field values on the quote line or the quote during calculation, like setting a discount, a special price or a custom field. I usually tell them apart from how the requirement is worded. If a packaging client says 'the shrink-wrap service must include pallets' or 'can't be sold with the eco box', that's a product rule. If they say 'the discount should be 5% when they order kitting with printing', that's a price rule. Both use conditions, both can use summary variables and lookup tables, and both have an evaluation order.
points: Product rule = configuration (what can be sold together)
Price rule = values (prices, discounts, fields) during calculation
Both support summary variables, lookup tables and evaluation order

q: What are the components of a price rule in CPQ?
alt: Explain price conditions and price actions
How do you build a price rule in Salesforce CPQ?
what is price condition and price action
What does evaluation scope mean on a price rule?
a: A price rule has three parts. First, Price Conditions decide when it fires. Each one compares a tested field, variable or formula against a value, and Conditions Met can be All, Any or Custom logic. Second, Price Actions decide what happens. Each writes a value into a target field on the quote line or quote, and that value can come from a static value, a field, a formula, a summary variable or a lookup table. Third, the rule settings: the Calculator Evaluation Event, which is On Initialization, Before Calculate, On Calculate or After Calculate, plus the Evaluation Order, the target object, and the Evaluation Scope, which is either the calculator or the configurator. For example, a rule might check that the product family is Packaging Services and quantity is at least 10,000, then write a discount into the line. One tip: I keep each rule to a single evaluation event for performance.
points: Conditions: tested field/variable/formula, Conditions Met All/Any/Custom
Actions: target field, value from static, field, formula, variable or lookup
Evaluation event, evaluation order, scope (calculator or configurator)

q: Can you explain the CPQ quote calculation sequence and where price rules run?
alt: What is the order of calculation in Salesforce CPQ?
When does On Initialization vs On Calculate vs After Calculate run?
explain cpq calculation sequence evaluation events
In what order does CPQ evaluate formula fields and price rules?
a: CPQ runs a fixed sequence every time it calculates. First it loads data from related records like products and costs. Then it runs On Initialization price rules and evaluates formula fields on lines, the quote and groups. Next come Before Calculate rules, then quantity calculation, like bundle component quantities, then On Calculate rules. After that CPQ applies its built-in pricing, like block prices, discount schedules and the price waterfall. Then After Calculate rules run, formula fields are re-evaluated, and finally group and quote totals are calculated. Inside one event, rules run by Evaluation Order and actions by their Order field, and CPQ tests all the conditions in an event before running any actions. Here's why it matters. Say a packaging quote has a rule that needs the volume discount result. On Calculate is too early, because discount schedules haven't applied yet, so I'd put it After Calculate. If there's a Quote Calculator Plugin, its hooks run at defined points around these stages.
points: Initialization rules -> formulas -> Before Calculate -> quantities -> On Calculate
Then built-in pricing (block, discount schedules) -> After Calculate -> formulas -> totals
Priority: event, then rule evaluation order, then action order
All conditions in an event are tested before any action runs

q: What are lookup tables in CPQ price rules and why use them?
alt: How does a lookup object work with price rules?
What is a lookup query in CPQ?
how to avoid creating hundreds of price rules in cpq
Explain price rule with lookup table
a: A lookup table lets a price rule pull values from a custom object instead of hard-coding them across lots of rules. Say a packaging manufacturer gives different discounts by region, product family and order size. I'd create a custom object, like a regional discount matrix, with fields such as Region, Product Family, Minimum Quantity and Discount. On the price rule I set the Lookup Object, then add Lookup Queries that match quote or line fields to the lookup fields, using operators like equals or less than. The price action then uses a source lookup field to write the matched value into the target field. So a West region quote for 20,000 corrugated boxes finds its row and gets that row's discount. The big win is maintenance. When the business changes a rate, they update a row in the table instead of asking an admin to create a new rule for every combination.
points: Custom object holds the matrix of values
Lookup Queries match quote/line fields to table fields
Price action writes from the matched row's field
Business maintains data rows instead of rules

q: What is a summary variable in Salesforce CPQ?
alt: How do summary variables work in CPQ?
How can a rule check the total quantity across all quote lines?
summary variable cpq example
What aggregate functions can summary variables use?
a: A summary variable aggregates values across quote lines so a rule can decide something at the quote level. You pick the target object, usually Quote Line, an aggregate function like Sum, Average, Min, Max or Count, the field to aggregate, and filters like Product Family equals Hardware. Then a price condition, a product rule error condition or a price action can use it. For example, a packaging company might sum the quantity of every line where the product family is Corrugated Boxes. Once that total crosses a threshold, a price rule gives an extra discount. Or a validation rule could require a quality inspection service when the total gets high enough. You can also combine two variables with a composite operator, like a boxes total minus a services total.
points: Aggregates: Sum, Average, Min, Max, Count with filters
Usable in price conditions, price actions and product rule conditions
Composite operators combine variables

q: Explain the CPQ pricing waterfall.
alt: What is list price, special price, regular price, customer price, partner price and net price?
How does CPQ go from list price to net price?
explain price waterfall in salesforce cpq
In what order are discounts applied in CPQ?
a: The price waterfall is the order CPQ goes through from the starting price to the final price on a quote line. It starts with Original Price from the price book, then List Price. Special Price applies things like contracted prices, option pricing or price rule overrides. Prorated Price adjusts subscription products for the quote's term. Regular Price applies volume discounts like discount schedules. Customer Price applies the rep's additional discount. Partner Price applies the partner discount, and Net Price applies the distributor discount. Then Net Price times quantity gives the Net Total. So say a sales manager asks why a packaging customer's carton price is so far below list. I walk down the waterfall with them: a contracted price set the Special Price, the volume tier set the Regular Price, and the rep's own discount sits in Customer Price. That's how I explain where every number came from.
points: Original -> List -> Special -> Prorated -> Regular
Regular -> Customer (additional discount) -> Partner -> Net
Net Total = Net Price x Quantity

q: What is a discount schedule in CPQ, and what is the difference between slab and range?
alt: Slab vs range discount schedule
How do volume discounts work in Salesforce CPQ?
what is slab pricing in cpq
Explain discount tiers in a CPQ discount schedule
a: A discount schedule gives volume or term-based discounts through tiers, and the type decides how the tiers apply. Say we quote pallet-packing services with two tiers: 0% up to 100 units and 10% above that. With Range, the whole quantity gets the discount of the tier it lands in, so if the customer orders 150, all 150 units get 10%. With Slab, each portion gets its own tier's rate, so the first 100 get 0% and the next 50 get 10%, and you end up with a blended price. Range is easier to explain to a customer. Slab avoids the cliff where ordering just one more unit suddenly drops the total. I'd also mention that schedules can be attached to the product, to a contracted price, or be term-based for subscriptions.
points: Range: entire quantity gets the matching tier's discount
Slab: each quantity band gets its own tier rate
Tier lower bound is inclusive, upper bound exclusive
Can be product-level, contracted-price-level or term-based

q: What is block pricing in Salesforce CPQ?
alt: How does block pricing work?
When would you use block pricing instead of per-unit pricing?
block price cpq example
How do you charge a flat price for a range of quantity in CPQ?
a: Block pricing charges a flat price for a quantity range instead of a per-unit price. You set the product's pricing method to Block and create Block Price records with a lower bound, upper bound and price. Say a packaging firm sells a monthly kitting service in bands: one fixed amount for 1 to 10 pallets and another for 11 to 25. If the customer needs 7 pallets, the line total is the 1-to-10 block price, not unit price times 7. If you add a custom OverageRate field to the Block Price object, the highest block can also charge a per-unit rate for quantities above it, so anything past 25 pallets is billed per unit. It suits packaged offerings like user packs or storage tiers, where the customer buys a band rather than an exact count.
points: Pricing Method = Block, with Block Price records
Line total = block price, not unit price x quantity
Custom OverageRate field charges per unit above the last block

q: What is cost-plus markup pricing in CPQ?
alt: How do you price a product from its cost in CPQ?
Explain the Cost pricing method
cost plus pricing salesforce cpq markup
How does markup work on a CPQ quote line?
a: Cost-plus markup prices a product from its cost instead of a fixed list price. I set the product's pricing method to Cost and create a Cost record with the unit cost. On the quote line, CPQ applies a markup, either a percentage or an amount, so the price is cost plus markup. Reps can adjust the markup if it's editable, or you can lock it. A good example is a packaging manufacturer reselling stretch film. The film cost moves every quarter, so instead of chasing a list price they store the cost and add a markup on top. It's common for services, resale items or hardware, where cost changes often and margin matters more than a list price. You can still layer discounts on top, and I'd pair it with approvals, for example requiring approval when the markup drops below an agreed level.
points: Pricing Method = Cost, with a Cost record
Price = cost + markup (percent or amount)
Pair with approvals on low markup or margin

q: What are contracted prices in Salesforce CPQ?
alt: How do you give one customer a special negotiated price?
What is a Contracted Price record?
account specific pricing in cpq
How are contracted prices generated from a contract?
a: Contracted prices are account-specific prices that override the normal price at the Special Price stage of the waterfall. A Contracted Price record sits on the account. It points to a product, or to a filter on product fields, and holds either a fixed price or a discount, with optional start and end dates and even its own discount schedule. You can create them by hand, or have them generated automatically when a contract is created, if the quote line or product is set to generate a contracted price. For example, say a food brand negotiates a fixed price for printed cartons for the year. Once that's a contracted price on their account, every new quote for that carton picks up the negotiated rate automatically. That's how we honour negotiated rates without building a separate price book for every customer.
points: Lives on the account; product-based or filter-based
Fixed price or discount, with effective dates
Can be auto-generated on contracting
Applied at Special Price stage

q: What is the Quote Line Editor in CPQ?
alt: What is QLE in Salesforce CPQ?
How do you control which columns appear in the quote line editor?
explain the cpq line editor
Where do reps add products to a CPQ quote?
a: The Quote Line Editor, or QLE, is the main CPQ screen. It's where reps add products, configure bundles, change quantities and discounts, group lines and calculate the quote. It runs CPQ's pricing engine, so when you click Calculate or Save, price rules, discount schedules and the waterfall get applied. So a rep quoting a packaging job adds the box bundle, sets the quantity, enters their discount, hits Calculate and sees the tiered price straight away. Admins control the visible columns through the line editor field set on the quote line object. They can add custom buttons and actions, enable line groups and segments, and control editability with field-level security or the Quote Calculator Plugin's visibility and editability hooks. One practical point: most CPQ performance complaints show up in the QLE, so keeping those field sets lean really helps.
points: Main UI for adding, configuring and pricing lines
Columns controlled by the line editor field set
Calculate/Save runs the pricing engine
Lean field sets help performance

q: What is the Quote Calculator Plugin in CPQ, and can you show an example?
alt: What is QCP in Salesforce CPQ?
Write a QCP that calculates margin on quote lines
how do you write javascript for the cpq calculator
What methods does the quote calculator plugin support?
a: The Quote Calculator Plugin, or QCP, is JavaScript that hooks into CPQ's calculation when declarative price rules aren't enough. You store the code on a Custom Script record, list the quote and line fields it uses, and register it in CPQ package settings under Plugins. It exports functions like onInit, onBeforeCalculate, onBeforePriceRules, onAfterPriceRules and onAfterCalculate. They receive the quote model and line models and return a Promise. There are also isFieldVisible and isFieldEditable hooks for the line editor. Say a packaging quote needs a value worked out by looking at every line. In one of those hooks I'd loop the lines and read and write fields by API name on line.record. The gotcha is that it runs both in the browser and in CPQ's server-side calculator, so it can't touch the DOM. And I only use the conn object when a query is really needed.
points: Stored on a Custom Script record, registered in package settings
Hooks: onInit, onBeforeCalculate, onBeforePriceRules, onAfterPriceRules, onAfterCalculate
Return a Promise; access fields by API name on .record
List every field used in the script's quote/line field lists

q: When would you use the Quote Calculator Plugin instead of price rules?
alt: QCP vs price rules, which is better?
Why not put all pricing logic in the QCP?
when is javascript plugin needed in cpq
What are the downsides of the quote calculator plugin?
a: I default to price rules, and only reach for QCP when the logic really can't be expressed declaratively. Price rules are admin-maintainable, visible in setup and easier to audit. QCP fits when I need loops across lines with complex math, logic that depends on other lines in ways summary variables can't handle, data from a query, or control over field visibility and editability in the line editor. For example, if a packaging manufacturer wants a tooling charge that depends on the exact mix of box sizes across all the lines, that's probably QCP territory. The trade-offs are real though. Admins can't easily read it, there's no built-in test framework like Apex has, only one plugin is active per org, and a bug can break every quote calculation. So I keep it small, version-control it, test with representative quotes, and document which logic lives where.
points: Default: declarative price rules
QCP: complex cross-line math, queries, field visibility/editability
Risks: one plugin per org, harder to maintain, can break all calculations

q: How do quote templates and document generation work in CPQ?
alt: How do you generate a quote PDF in Salesforce CPQ?
What are template sections and template content?
how to show a section only if certain products are on the quote
Explain CPQ quote template setup
a: A quote template defines the PDF or Word document CPQ generates from a quote. It's built from Template Content records, which can be HTML, Quote Terms, Line Items, or Custom using a Visualforce page, and you arrange those into Template Sections. Line Columns control which line fields print. A section can also be conditional through a Conditional Print Field. So for a packaging company, the warehousing services terms section only prints when there's a warehousing service on the quote. The rep clicks Preview or Generate Document, and CPQ creates a Quote Document record with the file. That can be emailed or sent for e-signature through integrations like DocuSign. q: What is CPQ Advanced Approvals and how is it different from standard approval processes?

How do you set up approvals for discounts in CPQ?
a: Advanced Approvals is a separate managed package, with the sbaa namespace, that adds richer approval logic for CPQ quotes. You build Approval Rules with Approval Conditions, assign approvers, and organise the rules into Approval Chains for sequential or parallel paths. Approvers can be dynamic, like the rep's manager taken from a field. Two features I'd call out. Smart approvals: after a resubmission, only the approvals affected by the change are requested again. And approval variables, which aggregate line data like the maximum discount. Say a packaging quote needs finance and the plant manager to approve. If the rep only changes something that triggered the plant manager's rule, finance isn't asked again. Standard approval processes also work, but they're linear, need separate processes for different scenarios, and re-request every approval when the quote is resubmitted.

q: How do amendments work in Salesforce CPQ?
alt: What happens when you amend a contract in CPQ?
How do you add licenses mid-term in CPQ?
explain cpq amendment co termination
Why can't I change the price of existing lines on an amendment quote?
a: An amendment changes an active contract mid-term. Say a customer has a 12-month contract for pallet storage, and six months in they want 20 more pallet spaces. From the contract you click Amend, and CPQ creates an amendment opportunity and quote with the existing subscriptions at their current quantities. The rep can increase or decrease quantities or add new products. Existing lines keep their original price, and only the change is charged. New and changed lines are prorated to co-terminate with the contract end date, so those 20 extra spaces are priced for the remaining six months. When the amendment is contracted, CPQ creates new subscription records for the delta instead of overwriting the old ones, which keeps a clear history.

q: How do renewals work in CPQ and what is the Renewal Pricing Method?
alt: Explain renewal forecast and renewal quoted
How does CPQ price a renewal quote?
renewal pricing method same list uplift
How do you automate renewal opportunities in CPQ?
a: Renewals continue a contract for another term. When the contract's Renewal Forecast checkbox is set, CPQ creates a renewal opportunity, and setting Renewal Quoted creates a renewal quote with the subscriptions that are due. Pricing depends on the Renewal Pricing Method on the account. Same keeps the previous price, List reprices from the current price book, and Uplift applies a percentage increase from the Renewal Uplift field. For example, if a packaging customer's warehousing contract renews with Uplift and a Renewal Uplift of 5%, the renewal quote comes in 5% higher automatically. You can also choose contract-based or asset-based renewal models, and use co-termination so several contracts renew together. In practice I automate setting Renewal Forecast when a contract is activated, so the pipeline always shows upcoming renewals.

q: How do subscriptions and proration work in Salesforce CPQ?

Explain subscription term and proration in CPQ
a: A subscription product in CPQ has Subscription Pricing set to Fixed Price or Percent of Total, a default subscription term, and a subscription type like renewable, one-time or evergreen. On the quote, CPQ compares the line's effective term with the product's default term to get a prorate multiplier. Say a packaging customer buys a managed warehousing service with a 12-month default term, but the quote runs for 18 months. The multiplier is 1.5, so they pay one and a half times the 12-month price. Package settings control the term unit and how partial periods are prorated, for example monthly, daily or a combination. When the quote is contracted, CPQ creates Subscription records on the contract, and those drive amendments and renewals. Percent of Total products, like support charged as a percentage of hardware, calculate from the lines they cover.

q: What are twin fields in Salesforce CPQ?

how to pass a custom field from quote line to opportunity product
Do I need a flow to copy fields from quote line to order product?
a: Twin fields are CPQ's way of copying custom field values between related objects without code. If a custom field with the same API name and a compatible data type exists on two objects in CPQ's flow, CPQ copies the value automatically. Say a packaging manufacturer has a Print Colours custom field on Product. If I create the same field on Quote Line, the value comes across when the product is added. The same field on Opportunity Product picks it up when the quote syncs, and it can carry on down to Order Product and Subscription. That saves writing flows for simple mappings. The catches: names must match exactly, the target field must be editable by the user, and each pair maps at a specific moment. So I always test the exact path the data needs to take.

q: What is multi-dimensional quoting (MDQ) in CPQ?

How do you quote different prices per year in CPQ?
what are segmented quote lines in cpq
How do ramp deals work in Salesforce CPQ?
a: Multi-dimensional quoting, or MDQ, lets one subscription line be split into time segments, like Year 1, Year 2 and Year 3, each with its own quantity, price or discount. You set it up by adding a Price Dimension to the product, with a type like Year, Quarter, Month, One-time or Custom. In the line editor the segments show up as columns. So if a packaging customer wants a three-year kitting contract that ramps up as their new product line grows, the rep enters a lower quantity for Year 1, higher ones after that, and gives a bigger first-year discount. Behind the scenes each segment is its own quote line tied to the dimension, and downstream each becomes its own subscription. It does add complexity, so before turning it on I check the impact on templates, price rules, renewals and reporting.

q: Your custom trigger on CPQ quote lines keeps hitting CPU time and SOQL limits when a quote is saved. How do you fix it?
alt: CPQ quote line trigger causing too many SOQL queries
How do you handle governor limits with CPQ triggers?
what is sbqq trigger control
Quote save fails with apex cpu time limit exceeded in CPQ
a: CPQ updates quote lines several times during one calculate and save, so a custom trigger on quote lines can run repeatedly and burn limits. First I check whether the logic belongs in a price rule or the calculator plugin, since those run inside the calculation. If a trigger is needed, I bulkify it, use a static set so each record is processed once per transaction, only act when relevant fields actually changed, and push heavy work into a Queueable. For bulk data fixes from Apex or a batch, I wrap the DML with SBQQ.TriggerControl.disable() and enable() so CPQ's own triggers don't recalculate on every chunk, and then recalculate the affected quotes afterwards in a controlled way.
points: Move logic to price rules or QCP where possible
Bulkify, guard against re-entry, check changed fields only
Offload heavy work to Queueable
SBQQ.TriggerControl.disable()/enable() for bulk updates

q: What is large quote mode in CPQ and how is it different from the normal calculation?

Why does CPQ calculate some quotes asynchronously?
legacy vs large quote mode cpq
How do you handle quotes with hundreds of lines in CPQ?
a: CPQ doesn't have one single switch called large quote mode. It's a set of package settings for big quotes. The main one is the Large Quote Threshold. Quotes with more lines than that value are treated as large, so the line editor sends only the essential quote lines and quote-scoped product rules are skipped, which helps avoid governor limit errors. Quote Batch Size controls how many lines are processed per batch on load and save. Enable Large Quote Experience changes the line editor layout so reps can move around big quotes more easily. Separately, CPQ can run calculations asynchronously through its calculation service, so reps may see totals update after a delay and have to wait before trusting them. Say a packaging manufacturer quotes its full range of SKUs to a retail chain. I'd tune those settings, but still keep field sets lean, price rules on a single event, and the QCP efficient.
points: Large Quote Threshold: above it, only essential lines sent and quote-scope product rules skipped
Quote Batch Size: lines per batch on load and save
Enable Large Quote Experience: easier QLE layout for big quotes
Still tune rules, field sets and QCP

bundle with required options and one support level

For items that must always be there, like the base license, I create product options marked Required and Selected, and Bundled if their price is included in the parent. For the support plan I create a feature called Support with Min Option Count 1 and Max Option Count 1, and put Standard, Premium and Enterprise under it as options, so the configurator forces exactly one choice. If one option should only be allowed with another, I add an option constraint, and only if the logic depends on quote values would I add a validation product rule.

q: The business wants a 10% discount automatically when the quantity is above 50 units. How would you implement it in CPQ?

Give 10 percent off if quantity greater than 50
discount schedule or price rule for quantity discount
How to apply a quantity based discount in CPQ
a: My first choice is a discount schedule, because it's built for exactly this. I'd create a Range discount schedule with two tiers, 0% for 1 to 50 units and 10% from 51 upwards, keeping in mind that the tier upper bound is exclusive, and attach it to the product. CPQ then applies it automatically at the Regular Price stage of the waterfall. If it must apply across many products, depend on other criteria like region, or use the total quantity across lines, I'd use a price rule instead: a condition on quantity greater than 50, or on a summary variable, and an action that sets Additional Discount to 10, evaluated On Calculate.

q: The business wants every renewal to increase automatically by 5% over last year's price. How do you set that up in CPQ?
alt: Renewal uplift of 5 percent
How to apply price increase on renewal quotes in CPQ
configure renewal uplift salesforce cpq
Annual price escalation on renewals
a: CPQ supports this out of the box. On the account, I set Renewal Pricing Method to Uplift, and I set Renewal Uplift (%) to 5 on the contract. When the renewal quote is generated, CPQ starts from the previous customer price and applies the 5% increase instead of repricing from the list. If the uplift should differ by product, it can also be set on individual subscriptions, and the subscription value takes precedence over the contract. I'd test with a multi-year contract, check how it interacts with MDQ segments and discounts, and confirm the renewal opportunity amount matches what finance expects.

q: A price rule you built isn't firing on the quote. How do you troubleshoot it?
alt: Why is my CPQ price rule not working?
Price action not updating the field
price rule not triggering in quote line editor
Debug a CPQ price rule that does nothing
a: I go through a checklist. First, is the rule active, and is the evaluation scope right, calculator versus configurator? Second, the evaluation event. If it runs On Initialization but depends on values calculated later, it won't see them. Third, the conditions: All versus Any, picklist values spelled exactly, and matching data types. Fourth, evaluation order and later stages, because another rule or a discount schedule may be overwriting my target field. Fifth, the target field has to be on the right object, editable, and not a formula. For lookup rules I check the lookup queries really match a row. A typical example: a packaging discount rule tests for 'Corrugated' but the picklist value is actually 'Corrugated Boxes', so it never fires. If the checklist doesn't find it, I simplify by removing conditions one at a time and recalculating in the line editor.
points: Active? Correct scope and evaluation event?
Conditions: All/Any, exact picklist values, data types
Something later overwriting the target field?
Target field editable, not a formula; lookup returns a match

q: Reps complain that the Quote Line Editor takes over a minute to calculate quotes with 400 or more lines. What would you do?
alt: CPQ quote is very slow to calculate
How to improve CPQ performance
quote line editor timeout large quotes
Optimise price rules and QCP for performance
a: I'd first measure where the time goes, using browser developer tools and debug logs, and count the active price rules, product rules, summary variables and QCP hooks. Typical fixes: give each price rule a single evaluation event, deactivate or merge redundant rules, and replace many similar rules with one lookup-table rule. I trim the line editor field set and remove unneeded formula fields on quote lines, especially cross-object ones. In the QCP I avoid queries inside loops and skip work when nothing relevant changed. I review custom triggers and flows on quote lines. If quotes are still large, I tune the Large Quote Threshold and Quote Batch Size package settings, and consider grouping or MDQ to reduce line counts.
points: Measure first: rules, variables, QCP, triggers
One evaluation event per rule; lookup tables over many rules
Lean field sets and fewer formula fields
Tune Large Quote Threshold and Quote Batch Size

q: If a quote has hardware products, it must also include a support product, otherwise the rep can't save. How would you build that?
alt: Block saving a quote without support
Quote level validation rule in CPQ using summary variables
require a product when another product family exists
How to force reps to add support with hardware
a: This is a validation product rule at quote scope. I'd create two summary variables: one counting quote lines where Product Family is Hardware, and one counting lines where Product Family is Support. Then I'd create a product rule of type Validation, scope Quote, evaluation event Save, with error conditions hardware count greater than zero and support count equal to zero, and Conditions Met set to All. The message tells the rep exactly what to add. If the business prefers auto-adding support instead of blocking, I'd make it a selection rule with an Add action. I'd also test with bundles, because bundle options are quote lines too.

How does a selection rule add products?
automatically include accessory in cpq bundle
Add a mounting kit whenever a display is selected
a: If both are inside the same bundle, the simplest way is a selection product rule with Product scope. The error condition checks that the triggering option is selected, and the product action is Add, pointing at the product to include, for example adding a mounting kit when a wall display is chosen. An evaluation event of Always or Edit makes it react as the rep configures. If the products aren't in a bundle, I can use a Quote-scope selection rule, or redesign them as a bundle with the extra item as a required option. The same rule type also supports Remove, Hide and Disable actions for incompatible choices.

q: A customer wants a three-year subscription with 100 users in year one, 150 in year two and 200 in year three, with a bigger discount in year one. How would you quote it in CPQ?
alt: Ramp deal with increasing users each year
Different quantity and discount per year in one quote
how to do a multi year ramp in salesforce cpq
Quote a three year deal with yearly segments
a: That's a classic multi-dimensional quoting use case. I'd add a yearly price dimension to the subscription product to make it MDQ, and set the quote's subscription term to 36 months. In the line editor the product then shows Year 1, Year 2 and Year 3 columns, where the rep enters 100, 150 and 200 users and a different discount for each segment. Each segment becomes its own line and later its own subscription, so billing and renewals follow the ramp. Without MDQ, the alternative is separate lines with staggered start and end dates, but that's harder for reps and reporting, so MDQ is cleaner when ramp deals are common.

q: What is Revenue Cloud Advanced?
alt: What is Salesforce Revenue Cloud?
What is Agentforce Revenue Management?
what is r c a in salesforce
What replaced CPQ in Salesforce?
a: Revenue Cloud Advanced, or RCA, is Salesforce's next-generation quote-to-cash product and the successor to Salesforce CPQ. It's part of Salesforce Revenue Cloud, which started out as Revenue Lifecycle Management, or RLM, and has also been branded Agentforce Revenue Management. The big difference from CPQ is that it isn't a managed package. It's built natively on the platform using standard objects like Quote, Order and Asset. It covers the lifecycle end to end: Product Catalog Management, Salesforce Pricing, Product Configurator, quotes and orders through Transaction Management, fulfillment with Dynamic Revenue Orchestrator, contracts, and with Revenue Cloud Billing, invoicing and payments. So for a packaging manufacturer, one platform takes a deal from the catalog, to a priced quote, to an order, to fulfillment, to the invoice. It's also API-first, so the same pricing and configuration can serve the Salesforce UI, a portal or an AI agent.
points: Successor to Salesforce CPQ
Part of Revenue Cloud (formerly Revenue Lifecycle Management; also branded Agentforce Revenue Management)
Native, standard objects, no managed package
